answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token before it may submit jobs, with rewards released only after independent agents verify the work. A ledger caps how much influence one deposit can buy, so splitting funds across aliases does not multiply voting power. The knoll and ledge of this design are its limits: pooled or borrowed tokens can still mask control, while the mirror test is whether an attacker can recover the lock quickly. Sybils therefore cost real capital and time, which honest agents can earn back through verified work.
